structures.title: Nominal sentence with no 'to be'
structures.explanation: A nominal sentence (الجملة الاسمية) links a definite subject to an indefinite predicate with no word for 'is/are' in the present. Just place the two nouns/adjectives together. The definite–indefinite contrast shows which is which.

structures.title: Verbal sentence in VSO order
structures.explanation: A verbal sentence (الجملة الفعلية) begins with the verb, then the subject, then the object. The verb stays singular even before a plural subject when it comes first. This VSO order is the classical default.

structures.title: Forming a yes/no question
structures.explanation: Put هَلْ (or the prefix أ) in front of a normal statement to turn it into a yes/no question; word order does not change. The answer is نَعَم (yes) or لا (no).

structures.title: Negating each tense correctly
structures.explanation: Each tense has its own negator: لا before the present, لم plus the jussive for the past, لن plus the subjunctive for the future. The verb form shifts to match the particle.

structures.pattern: noun vs ال + noun + agreeing adj
structures.title: Definite/indefinite with adjectives
structures.explanation: An indefinite noun has no article; the definite adds ال. The adjective follows the noun and must match it in definiteness, gender, number, and case. Both words carry ال or neither does.

structures.title: Past 'to be' with كان
structures.explanation: To say 'was/were', use كان before the predicate, which then takes the accusative case (ـاً). The subject stays nominative. كان also expresses 'used to' with a following present verb.

structures.title: Possession with iḍāfa
structures.explanation: Two nouns placed side by side express 'X of Y'. The first noun drops ال and tanwīn; only the last noun may take ال, and it sits in the genitive case. No word for 'of' is used.

structures.title: Negating a nominal sentence
structures.explanation: ليس means 'is not' and negates a present nominal sentence. Like كان, it puts the predicate in the accusative while the subject stays nominative. It conjugates for person and gender.

structures.title: Comparative 'more ... than'
structures.explanation: The comparative uses the fixed أَفْعَل pattern followed by مِنْ ('than'). This one form is invariable — it does not change for gender or number of the subject.
structures.ex1_ref: The book is bigger than the pen.
structures.ex2_ref: She is smarter than her brother.

structures.title: Saying 'I want to ...'
structures.explanation: To express 'want to do', use أُريد followed by أَنْ and a verb in the subjunctive (ending -a). أَنْ links the two verbs, where English uses the infinitive 'to'.

structures.title: Expressing obligation 'must'
structures.explanation: يَجِبُ أَنْ plus a subjunctive verb means 'must/have to'. It is impersonal, so the person is shown only by the following verb. Use يَجِبُ عَلَيَّ أَنْ to stress 'I' specifically.

structures.title: Giving a reason with 'because'
structures.explanation: لِأَنَّ ('because') joins a result to its cause and, like its sister إنّ, puts the following subject noun or pronoun suffix in the accusative. It always introduces a full clause.
structures.ex1_ref: I stay home because I am sick.
structures.ex2_ref: He succeeded because he worked hard.

structures.title: Talking about the future
structures.explanation: Prefix سـ (near) or سَوْفَ (further off) to a present-tense verb to make the future. Nothing else changes. سَوْفَ can also carry a stronger sense of certainty.
structures.ex1_ref: I will go to the market tomorrow.

structures.title: Relative clause 'the one who/that'
structures.explanation: Use الَّذي (m.) or الَّتي (f.) after a definite noun to attach a describing clause. The relative pronoun agrees with the noun in gender and number. With an indefinite noun, drop the pronoun entirely.
structures.ex1_ref: The man who lives here is a doctor.
structures.ex2_ref: The magazine that I read is useful.

structures.title: Real conditional 'if ...'
structures.explanation: إذا introduces a likely/real condition, usually with a past-tense verb that reads as present or future. The result clause follows, often with a future verb. Use لَوْ instead for hypothetical/unreal conditions.
structures.ex1_target: إذا كانَ عِنْدي وَقْتٌ، سَأَتَّصِلُ بِكَ.
structures.ex1_ref: If I have time, I will call you.

structures.title: Superlative 'the most ...'
structures.explanation: Make the superlative by adding ال to the أَفْعَل form, or by making it the first term of an iḍāfa followed by a singular genitive noun. Both express 'the -est'.
structures.ex1_ref: He is the tallest in the class.
structures.ex2_ref: It is the most beautiful city.
